scope: Full close reading of the pinned local author arXiv v1, 17 physical PDF pages including references, with selected figure/table visual checks. No GPU/inference experiments, upstream implementation audit or independent reproduction.
title: Herschel: Continuous Optimization of Production LLM Inference through On-Demand Profiling
publication_identity: Author arXiv preprint v1, dated 2026-09-30 on the PDF front page. Conference publication identity not verified.
method: Read all page-preserving PDFKit text and inspect selected local PDFKit-rendered pages. Observations are paraphrases. Source locations use 1-based inclusive text lines and SHA-256 of each newline-normalized line block, avoiding extensive copied excerpts. PDF is authoritative for two-column reading order, figures and tables.

observations.finding: Pinned arXiv v1 dated 2026-09-30, Alibaba Group; authors and title read from the PDF. Conference publication identity is not established by this audit.
Production MaaS continuous optimization combines runtime-attached profiling, dependency/pattern analysis and agent-driven implementation experiments. It is a direct neighbor of the proposed project.
Experts review candidate changes; canary validation and staged rollout are explicitly outside the Herschel system in Figure 3. Serving-SLO and correctness monitoring gate wider rollout.

The no-engine-change/no-restart claim applies to profiler attachment. Runtime integration of a candidate implementation is followed by review and deployment; this text does not establish arbitrary in-place hot replacement of engine state.

Initial entry uses ptrace on a selected thread with stack exclusions, redirects pthread_create to a loader that calls dlopen, then restores the application thread before waiting. Later control uses a socket.
Stop or lease expiry ends recording and drains output. Probe reclamation/reuse waits for safe callback/call lifetimes; CUDA transitions gate entry and drain tracked work.

A resident CPython frame-evaluation router records selected call intervals and supported object fields. Intervals include native work and waiting; engine-specific readers capture dimensions and token counts.

CUPTI supplies CUDA Runtime intervals and device kernels, memory and synchronization activities. Correlation IDs and device/stream identifiers connect submissions to execution; vendor adapters cover other accelerators.

The control plane samples instances and times by serving conditions, with canary collections and concurrency limits. Typical initial windows last 30 seconds; production samples contain at least ten complete inference steps, median over 700.
Analyzer reconstructs operator intervals/shapes, graph replay relationships and dependency paths. SOL uses max(MFU, MBU); graph padding and unresolved reconstruction are retained in the analysis.
Analysis follows communication, control/synchronization, state reuse and output consumers, using object identity and code semantics to distinguish removable work from required state updates.

More than 20,000 performance-related PR/CR records, expert knowledge and production investigations inform 35 patterns: 25 engine patterns in eight categories and ten operator patterns in three categories.
Hotness ranks estimated recoverable critical-path fractions across shapes/workloads, weighted by fleet GPU-hours. This is an opportunity estimate, not a validated performance gain.

Missing evidence leaves a mechanism unresolved. Analyzer requests expert-approved supplementary collection and carries source, changes and applicability conditions of reference fixes into experiments.

Controlled experiments typically use 8–32 idle or revocable accelerators, including P/D resources for disaggregated serving. Reduced scale must preserve triggering conditions/dependencies and expose the original issue; interrupted trials rerun after preemption.

Agents edit, build and test with correctness/performance feedback and a fixed baseline workload/settings. High-overhead profiling is disabled for comparisons. Budget, refuted hypotheses and stalled progress govern stopping.

Actions include KV-transfer overlap, valid state reuse, speculative-work pruning, asynchronous KV control and pre-dispatch DP metadata. Kernel agents optimize production shapes/dtypes/layouts, then reevaluate complete operators and serving workloads.

Overhead hosts have 8 H20s, two 48-core Xeon 8469C CPUs and 1 TiB DRAM, CUDA 13, PyTorch 2.13 and vLLM 0.29. Latency tests colocate P/D and use BF16 Qwen3-32B TP2 / Qwen3-235B-A22B TP8, input 4096/8192, output 512 and concurrency 32/64.

Hprof-full active-collection overhead is reported below 0.5% TTFT and 7% TPOT. Hprof-python without accelerator tracing reports median/P95 TPOT overhead below 1.5%. These are active-window measurements, not fleet-wide long-term overhead.
Hprof-full reports 0.12–0.46 CPU cores, 2.3–2.8 GiB peak RSS and 1.5–8.8 MiB/s trace. At the highest measured rate a 30-second session produces approximately 265 MiB.

On Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Python call counts agree 99.2% and immediate-parent relations 99.98%; separate GPU timelines have identical kernel order with median/P95 relative duration difference 1.6%/10%. These are record-fidelity results, not diagnosis accuracy.
Fifty attach–collect–detach cycles on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B show no observed worker hang or inference interruption in the monitored stages. This is a bounded empirical test.

Six months, approximately 17,000 traces, over 120 model variants, more than ten accelerator types and dozens of clusters. More than 3,900 / 23% of collected traces match at least one pattern; this is not a fleet improvement or diagnostic precision statistic.

Four representative deployment scopes are approximately 50, 50, 100 and 30 deployments. The DP-coordination row explicitly labels the upstream-port throughput result as offline testing; cases have distinct measurement scopes.

Supplementary EngineCore/workId evidence links delayed dispatch to synchronous KV-object creation. Creation is overlapped with model execution while saving still waits for success. Short-context prefill throughput improves 3.3% on GLM-5.2 and 3.3–5.7% including three Qwen models; change deployed.

Agent moves DP coordination ahead of Worker dispatch while distinguishing hybrid-attention PD handoff tails from equally sized ordinary prefill chunks, preserving recurrent state, tail sampling, idle ranks, target/draft plans and graph/fusion eligibility.
Figure 10 labels the original Hybrid adaptation +766/-150. The subsequent upstream port has a final runtime diff +707/-32 and tests +692/-1; they are separate revisions.

The original Hybrid patch is deployed. Subsequent-port offline tests on eight XPU-A devices report 6.0%, 4.8%, 2.5% throughput gains for 35B/122B/397B Qwen models, each the mean of two maximum observed paired gains at concurrency 32 and 128.

Prefill must build reusable target/drafter prefix/recurrent state. It removes later MTP 2/3 forwards while retaining the full first forward, because Decode drafts/verifies locally. Further intra-MTP1 prediction pruning remains an opportunity. Deployed typical short-context TTFT reduction is about 6%.
At a production Qwen3-4B shape on XPU-C, repeated Q/K layout conversions motivate one-time Q conversion/reuse and compatible K loads. Measured PA operator time falls 60.9%, SOL rises 7.3% to 18.7%.
Roughly 8–32% lower end-to-end TPOT combines the PA fix with KV-preparation, intermediate-copy and host-submission changes; it is not attributable solely to the PA kernel.
PC/PM sampling trials exceeded the online overhead budget; instruction-level analysis uses offline Nsight Compute.

Detected overhead can yield no repeatable serving gain. Failed trials retain diagnosis/implementation/workload distinctions. Engine-object readers had five releases over six months as internal layouts changed.

Production profiling, idle-capacity experiments and PD-aware agent changes already overlap the project. Proposed joint runtime/replacement action selection, explicit router/Mooncake publication/rotation and fixed-resource cumulative-goodput evaluation need their own implementation and comparison evidence.

interpretation_limits: Profiler attachment without engine restart is not evidence of arbitrary in-place deployment of optimized engine/kernel code.
Idle/revocable experiment capacity and disaggregated P/D resources are explicit; they must not be marked absent in a feature table.
Herschel covers concrete PD state semantics. Absence of an explicit router/Mooncake replacement protocol in this paper does not establish absence in uninspected implementation.

The paper does not specify a mandatory optimizer model/API endpoint or a contract that the optimized production service supplies its own agent inference. Do not infer backend restrictions or uniqueness from this omission.
Reported active-window overhead, fidelity agreement, trace-pattern hit rate, individual case gains and cumulative fleet business benefit are different metrics.
Agent iteration budgets are described, but this paper does not provide a fixed-three-node runtime-versus-replacement ablation or a complete longitudinal cost/goodput account for the proposed project.
PDF references are not independent verification of the publication identity or implementation claims of cited works.
Existing audit artifacts, framework source SHAs and the unimplemented status of this project remain unchanged.
